events.text:
## Recommendation
- Go to St. Joseph first. It's the best of the four for the week, though I'd still rate it only average.
- If St. Joseph is crowded or closed, pick South Haven or Grand Haven. I'd expect both to be slow to fair.
- Plan for deep water. Reports put boat fish at 100 feet or more, so pier action may depend on a wind shift that brings cold water in.
- Bring spoons. Spoons were the most-cited lure in recent reports, and orange and green were the colors that worked. Meat rigs and flies also produced in June.

**Ratings for pier salmon this week (my estimate, not a report):**
- St. Joseph: 2 (average)
- South Haven: 1 (below average)
- Grand Haven: 1 (below average)
- Muskegon: 1 (below average)

## Why
- St. Joseph ranks first because its most recent boat report was the best of the four: average quality, with boat anglers finding fish well beyond 120 feet (St. Joseph, 2023-07-05).
- I'd expect the piers to trail the boats, because no pier salmon reports exist for these ports and the reports that do exist describe boat fishing in deep water.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon get 1s because their newest reports are older (June 21 and June 7) and were slow or only fair, and the current wind shows little upwelling (Grand Haven and South Haven each show 0 hours of upwelling wind in the last 3 days).
- Past July weeks with similar water (about 70 F) were mostly slow to fair, so I'd expect an average-or-below pier outing unless a north or east wind brings cold water in.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (the newest report is 13 days old for St. Joseph and South Haven, 27 days old for Grand Haven, and 41 days old for Muskegon):
- South Haven, 2023-07-05: boat quality 1, fish caught in about 100 feet, mostly on spoons. "Most fish were caught on spoons."
- St. Joseph, 2023-07-05: boat quality 2, "Boat anglers were fishing well beyond 120 feet of water."
- Grand Haven, 2023-06-21: boat quality 2, salmon 35 to 90 feet down in 65 to 160 feet of water; orange spoons and green or yellow meat rigs worked.
- Muskegon, 2023-06-07: boat quality 1, "Boat anglers were finding the salmon action to be slow." Fish were 30 to 100 feet down in 70 to 180 feet of water.
- None of the recent salmon reports for these four ports described pier or shore fishing.

**Past seasons** (similar water temperature, about 70 F; general history, not this week):
- July 2022 reports for these ports were mostly slow (quality 0 to 1), with fish deep (100+ feet) and spoons or flies doing the work (St. Joseph, 2022-07-06; Grand Haven, 2022-07-14; Muskegon, 2022-07-14).

**Conditions now:**
- The conditions tool returned a backtest summary for the week before 2023-07-18, not live data. The figures below are from that week.
- Buoy surface water: St. Joseph 71 F, South Haven 71 F, Grand Haven 68 F, Muskegon 68 F.
- Satellite surface water near the piers (satellite, not measured): St. Joseph 72 F, South Haven 72 F, Grand Haven 70 F, Muskegon 69 F.
- Upwelling wind in the last 3 days: St. Joseph 4 hours, South Haven 0, Grand Haven 0, Muskegon 1.
- Average wind was 7 to 9 mph, with gusts to about 30 mph.
- Per the Michigan Sea Grant guidance, north-to-east wind of 8+ mph is what drives upwelling toward the piers. None was present in the last 3 days.

## Caveats
- The newest reports are 13 to 41 days old, and none are pier reports. These ratings are my inference from boat reports and current conditions, so treat them as low-confidence.
- Current conditions are from a backtest summary, not live data. I could not get a live forecast or the modeled pierhead temperature, so check the wind and water before you go.
- The piers can change quickly. A few hours of north-to-east wind at 8+ mph could cool the water near the piers and improve the fishing, especially at St. Joseph.
- If you can, check the pier at dawn or dusk and look for cold water (a sharp drop in the surface temperature).

## Sources
- St. Joseph and South Haven, week of 2023-07-05: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- Grand Haven and South Haven, week of 2023-06-21: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3614332
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, week of 2023-06-07: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/35ed629
- Past-season comparisons: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31f444a
